subproblem.title: Flat convergence implies weak convergence (Simon 7.2, 'if' part)
subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P open, and T, T_j ∈ D_n(U) (j ∈ ℕ) arbitrary currents. Suppose that for every open W ⊂⊂ U (W open, closure W compact and contained in U) the flat pseudodistance d_W(T_j, T) = flatDistance W (T_j) T = inf{M_W(S) + M_W(R) : R ∈ D_{n+1}(U), S ∈ D_n(U) integer multiplicity, T_j − T = ∂R + S} tends to 0 in [0, ∞]. Then T_j ⇀ T, i.e. T_j(ω) → T(ω) for every ω ∈ D^n(U).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Eucl P)), IsOpen U → ∀ (T : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (Tj : ℕ → GeometricCurrentOn U n), (∀ W, CompactlyContainedOpen W U → Tendsto (fun j => flatDistance W (Tj j) T) atTop (𝓝 0)) → WeaklyConvergesOn Tj T
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Simon Ch. 6, proof of 7.2, first sentence (“the 'if' part of the theorem is trivial: for a given W ⊂⊂ U, d_W(T_j,T) → 0 evidently implies (T_j − T)(ω) → 0 for any fixed ω ∈ D^n(U) with spt ω ⊆ W”). This is Step 1 of the parent proof, written out. No integrality and no mass bounds are used.

Notation. For α ∈ Λ^k(ℝ^P) let |α| := covectorEuclideanNorm α = (Σ_I α(e_I)²)^{1/2}, the sum over strictly increasing I : Fin k → Fin P, with e_I := (e_{I(1)},…,e_{I(k)}). For a test form η ∈ D^k(U) let ‖η‖ := sup_x |η(x)|. This is finite: x ↦ |η(x)| is continuous (square root of a finite sum of squares of the continuous functions x ↦ η(x)(e_I)) and vanishes outside the compact set tsupport η.

1. (|·| is a norm on Λ^k.) |cα| = |c|·|α|, and |α| = 0 implies α = 0. Indeed an alternating k-linear map is determined by its values on the increasing basis tuples e_I: expand the arguments in the standard basis by multilinearity; terms with a repeated basis vector vanish, and the others equal ±α(e_I) by alternation.

2. (Mass bound.) Let X ∈ D_k(U), W ⊆ ℝ^P any set and η ∈ D^k(U) with tsupport η ⊆ W. Then ENNReal.ofReal |X(η)| ≤ M_W(X) · ENNReal.ofReal ‖η‖.
   Proof: if ‖η‖ = 0 then η = 0 by step 1, so X(η) = 0. Otherwise put c := ‖η‖ > 0. The forms η/c and −η/c belong to D^k(U), have tsupport ⊆ W and satisfy |±η(x)/c| ≤ 1 for all x; that is, they belong to massAdmissibleOn U k W. By GeometricCurrentOn.le_massOn, ofReal(±X(η)/c) ≤ M_W(X); hence ofReal |X(η)| ≤ c · M_W(X).

3. (Choice of W.) Fix ω ∈ D^n(U) and let K := tsupport ω, a compact subset of U. Choose δ > 0 with cthickening(2δ, K) ⊆ U: if K = ∅ or U = ℝ^P any δ works; otherwise the continuous function infDist(·, ℝ^P ∖ U) is positive on K and attains a positive minimum 3δ there. Let W := thickening(δ, K). Then:
   - W is open, and closure W ⊆ cthickening(δ, K) ⊆ U;
   - closure W is closed and bounded, hence compact, so CompactlyContainedOpen W U;
   - tsupport(dω) ⊆ tsupport ω = K ⊆ W (tsupport_exteriorDerivative_subset), where dω = exteriorDerivativeTestOn U n ω.

4. (Near-optimal decompositions.) Let ε > 0. By hypothesis flatDistance W (T_j) T → 0 in [0, ∞], so there is j₀ with flatDistance W (T_j) T < ENNReal.ofReal ε for all j ≥ j₀. Now flatDistance W (T_j) T is the infimum of M_W(S) + M_W(R) over integer multiplicity R ∈ D_{n+1}(U), S ∈ D_n(U) with T_j(η) − T(η) = ∂R(η) + S(η) for all η ∈ D^n(U). So iInf_lt_iff gives, for each j ≥ j₀, such R_j, S_j with M_W(S_j) + M_W(R_j) < ofReal ε. In particular M_W(R_j) and M_W(S_j) are finite and < ofReal ε.

5. (Estimate.) Take η := ω and use ∂R_j(ω) = R_j(dω) (GeometricCurrentOn.boundary_apply). Step 2 (with k = n + 1, η = dω, and with k = n, η = ω) gives, for j ≥ j₀,
|T_j(ω) − T(ω)| = |R_j(dω) + S_j(ω)| ≤ |R_j(dω)| + |S_j(ω)| ≤ M_W(R_j)·‖dω‖ + M_W(S_j)·‖ω‖ ≤ ε (‖dω‖ + ‖ω‖).
Since the masses are finite, the inequalities of step 2 may be read in ℝ.

6. (Conclusion.) Since ε > 0 is arbitrary and ‖dω‖ + ‖ω‖ is a fixed finite number, T_j(ω) → T(ω). As ω ∈ D^n(U) was arbitrary, WeaklyConvergesOn Tj T. ∎
proof_key_steps: Mass bound |X(η)| ≤ M_W(X)·sup|η| for tsupport η ⊆ W, by rescaling ±η into the admissible set of M_W.
For ω ∈ D^n(U) take W := thickening δ (tsupport ω) ⊂⊂ U, which contains tsupport ω ⊇ tsupport dω.
flatDistance W (T_j) T < ε yields integer multiplicity R_j, S_j with T_j − T = ∂R_j + S_j and M_W(S_j) + M_W(R_j) < ε (iInf_lt_iff).
|T_j(ω) − T(ω)| = |R_j(dω) + S_j(ω)| ≤ ε(‖dω‖ + ‖ω‖), so T_j(ω) → T(ω) for every ω.

The ENNReal infimum argument supplies decompositions whose evaluations tend to zero, without assuming integrality or mass bounds on T and Tj.

subproblem.title: Mass of τ(M, θ, ξ) equals ∫_{M∩W} θ dH^n (Simon 3.2(3))
subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P open, (M, θ, ξ) a rectifiable triple in U of dimension n (IsRectifiableTriple U n M θ ξ), and T ∈ D_n(U) with T(ω) = ∫_M θ⟨ω, ξ⟩ dH^n (tauAction n M θ ξ ω) for every ω ∈ D^n(U). Then for every open W ⊆ ℝ^P, M_W(T) = ∫_{M∩W} θ dH^n in [0, ∞], i.e. T.massOn W = ∫⁻ x in M ∩ W, ENNReal.ofReal (θ x) ∂μHE[n].
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Eucl P)), IsOpen U → ∀ (T : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (M : Set (Eucl P)) (θ : Eucl P → ℝ) (ξ : Eucl P → NVector (Eucl P) n), IsRectifiableTriple U n M θ ξ → (∀ ω : TestFormOn U n, T ω = tauAction n M θ ξ ω) → ∀ W : Set (Eucl P), IsOpen W → T.massOn W = ∫⁻ x in M ∩ W, ENNReal.ofReal (θ x) ∂(μHE[n] : Measure (Eucl P))
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Simon Ch. 6, Remark 3.2(3) (M_W(τ(M,θ,ξ)) = ∫_{M∩W} θ dH^n for open W ⊆ U) and 2.7–2.8 (μ_T(W) = M_W(T)). The statement is used for real positive θ (rectifiable triples), as in the parent's preliminary (P1). The proof below is the standard duality argument.

Notation. H := μHE[n]. For α ∈ Λ^n(ℝ^P) and strictly increasing I : Fin n → Fin P put α_I := α(e_I), and |α| := covectorEuclideanNorm α = (Σ_I α_I²)^{1/2}. This is a Euclidean norm on the finite-dimensional space Λ^n, since an alternating map vanishing on all e_I is 0. For a test form ω, ‖ω‖ := sup_x |ω(x)|. For each I let dx^I ∈ Λ^n be the covector with (dx^I)_J = δ_{IJ} (wedge of coordinate functionals), so α = Σ_I α_I dx^I.

1. (CB) (Cauchy–Binet bound; self-contained.) Let τ = (τ₁,…,τ_n) be orthonormal in ℝ^P and ζ := ±simpleNVector τ, so ζ(α) = ±α(τ₁,…,τ_n). Let A_{jk} := ⟨τ_j, e_k⟩ and, for strictly increasing I, let A_I be the n×n minor of A on the columns I.
   (a) For every α ∈ Λ^n, α(τ) = Σ_I α(e_I) det A_I. Expand τ_j = Σ_k A_{jk} e_k by multilinearity; terms with a repeated basis vector vanish by alternation; group the remaining terms by their increasing rearrangement I, the sign of the sorting permutation producing det A_I.
   (b) Σ_I (det A_I)² = 1. Apply (a) to the alternating form α₀(v₁,…,v_n) := det(⟨τ_i, v_j⟩)_{i,j} (the wedge of the functionals ⟨τ_i, ·⟩), for which α₀(e_I) = det A_I and α₀(τ) = det(⟨τ_i, τ_j⟩) = 1.
   Consequences: by Cauchy–Schwarz in the coordinates (α(e_I))_I, |ζ(α)| ≤ |α| for every α ∈ Λ^n. The covector α^ζ := Σ_I ζ(dx^I) dx^I depends linearly on ζ and satisfies ζ(dx^I) = ±det A_I; hence |α^ζ| = 1 and ζ(α^ζ) = Σ_I (det A_I)² = 1. For n = 0 these claims are immediate (ζ(α) = ±α(), |α| = |α()|). For n > P there is no orthonormal n-frame, so the orientation condition of IsRectifiableTriple forces H(M) = 0 and every statement below holds trivially.

2. (Inequality ≤.) Let ω be admissible for M_W(T), i.e. ω ∈ D^n(U), tsupport ω ⊆ W and |ω(x)| ≤ 1 for all x. By the orientation condition of IsRectifiableTriple, for H-a.e. x ∈ M, ξ(x) = ±simpleNVector τ(x) with τ(x) orthonormal. So by step 1 (CB), |ξ(x)(ω(x))| ≤ |ω(x)| ≤ 1_W(x), since ω = 0 outside tsupport ω ⊆ W. The integrand θ ξ(ω) is integrable on M: it is bounded by θ·1_{M∩tsupport ω}, and tsupport ω is a compact subset of U. Hence ofReal(T(ω)) = ofReal(∫_M θ ξ(ω) dH) ≤ ∫⁻_M ofReal(θ |ξ(ω)|) dH ≤ ∫⁻_{M∩W} ofReal θ dH. Taking the supremum over admissible ω gives M_W(T) ≤ ∫⁻_{M∩W} ofReal θ dH.

3. (Inequality ≥: reduction to compact sets.) V := W ∩ U is open and M ∩ W = M ∩ V, since M ⊆ U. Let K_k := {x : |x| ≤ k, infDist(x, ℝ^P ∖ V) ≥ 1/k} (or K_k := B̄_k(0) if V = ℝ^P; K_k := ∅ if V = ∅). These sets are compact, increasing, contained in V, and ⋃_k K_k = V. Since θ is a.e.-strongly measurable on each M ∩ K_k, monotone convergence gives ∫⁻_{M∩V} ofReal θ dH = sup_k ∫⁻_{M∩K_k} ofReal θ dH. So it suffices to show: for every compact K ⊆ V and every ε > 0 there is ω admissible for M_W(T) with T(ω) ≥ ∫_{M∩K} θ dH − ε. Note ∫_{M∩K} θ dH < ∞ by the integrability condition.

4. (A finite measure.) Fix K and ε. If K = ∅ the claim holds with ω := 0 (ofReal(T(0)) = 0 = ∫_{M∩∅} θ dH); assume K ≠ ∅. Choose δ₀ > 0 with K' := cthickening(δ₀, K) ⊆ V (possible since K is compact and V open); then K' is a compact subset of U. Let ν := θ H⌞(M ∩ K'), a finite Borel measure since θ is integrable on M ∩ K'. For 0 < δ ≤ δ₀ put V_δ := thickening(δ, K) ⊆ K'. The sets V_δ ∖ K decrease to ∅ as δ ↓ 0 (K is closed), so ν(V_δ ∖ K) → 0; fix δ ∈ (0, δ₀] with ν(V_δ ∖ K) < ε/4.

5. (Target field.) For H-a.e. x ∈ M put β(x) := α^{ξ(x)} (step 1, (CB)), so |β(x)| = 1 and ξ(x)(β(x)) = 1; put β := 0 elsewhere. β is ν-a.e. strongly measurable: it is a fixed linear function of ξ on the full-measure set where ξ(x) is a unit simple n-vector.

6. (Continuous approximation.) β·1_K is ν-integrable and |β 1_K| ≤ 1.
   - Density: compactly supported continuous functions are dense in L¹(ν; Λ^n), because ν is a finite Borel measure on ℝ^P and hence regular (MeasureTheory.Integrable.exists_hasCompactSupport_integral_sub_le). That lemma measures the error in Lean's operator norm on Λ^n, which is equivalent to |·| on this finite-dimensional space; the equivalence constant is absorbed into the tolerance. So there is γ₀ ∈ C_c(ℝ^P; Λ^n) with ∫ |γ₀ − β 1_K| dν < ε/4.
   - Truncation: let π(α) := α / max(1, |α|), the nearest-point retraction onto the closed unit ball of the Euclidean norm |·|; π is continuous, 1-Lipschitz and π(0) = 0. Let χ₀ ∈ C_c(ℝ^P) with 0 ≤ χ₀ ≤ 1, χ₀ = 1 on K and tsupport χ₀ ⊆ V_δ. Put γ := χ₀ · (π ∘ γ₀).
   Then γ is continuous with compact tsupport ⊆ V_δ, and |γ| ≤ 1. Moreover |γ − β 1_K| ≤ |γ₀ − β 1_K| pointwise: on K, |π(γ₀) − π(β)| ≤ |γ₀ − β| because |β| ≤ 1; off K, |γ| ≤ |π(γ₀)| ≤ |γ₀|. Thus ∫ |γ − β 1_K| dν < ε/4.

7. (Smoothing.) Let ρ_σ (σ > 0) be a standard mollifier (smooth, ≥ 0, ∫ ρ_σ = 1, support in B_σ(0)) and ω_σ := γ * ρ_σ, the convolution of the Λ^n-valued continuous function γ. Choose σ₀ > 0 with cthickening(σ₀, tsupport γ) ⊆ V_δ; this is possible since tsupport γ is compact and V_δ open, and also covers V_δ = ℝ^P. For 0 < σ < σ₀:
   - ω_σ is smooth, and tsupport ω_σ is compact and ⊆ V_δ;
   - |ω_σ(x)| ≤ ∫ ρ_σ(x − y) |γ(y)| dy ≤ 1, by convexity of the norm;
   - ω_σ → γ uniformly as σ → 0, by uniform continuity of γ.
   Fix such σ with sup |ω_σ − γ| · ν(ℝ^P) < ε/4 and let ω := ω_σ. Then ω ∈ D^n(U) (as V_δ ⊆ V ⊆ U), tsupport ω ⊆ V_δ ⊆ W and |ω| ≤ 1, so ω is admissible for M_W(T).

8. (Estimate.) Since ω = 0 off V_δ ⊆ K',
T(ω) = ∫_M θ ξ(ω) dH = ∫ ξ(ω) dν = ∫_K ξ(β) dν + ∫_K ξ(ω − β) dν + ∫_{V_δ∖K} ξ(ω) dν.
   - The first term is ν(K) = ∫_{M∩K} θ dH, because ξ(x)(β(x)) = 1 for H-a.e. x ∈ M.
   - By step 1 (CB), |ξ(x)(α)| ≤ |α| for H-a.e. x ∈ M. So the second term is ≥ −∫_K |ω − β| dν ≥ −∫ |ω − γ| dν − ∫ |γ − β 1_K| dν > −ε/4 − ε/4.
   - The third term is ≥ −ν(V_δ ∖ K) > −ε/4.
   Hence T(ω) > ∫_{M∩K} θ dH − ε, and M_W(T) ≥ ofReal(T(ω)) (GeometricCurrentOn.le_massOn).

9. (Conclusion.) By steps 3–8, M_W(T) ≥ ∫⁻_{M∩K} ofReal θ dH for every compact K ⊆ V, hence M_W(T) ≥ ∫⁻_{M∩W} ofReal θ dH. With step 2, T.massOn W = ∫⁻ x in M ∩ W, ofReal(θ x) ∂H. ∎
proof_key_steps: Cauchy–Binet (self-contained): for ξ = ±τ₁∧…∧τ_n with τ orthonormal, |ξ(α)| ≤ |α|, and the linear dual unit covector α^ξ satisfies ξ(α^ξ) = 1.
≤: every admissible ω gives T(ω) ≤ ∫_{M∩W} θ dH^n.
≥: exhaust W ∩ U by compacts K; approximate β·1_K (β = α^ξ) in L¹(θH^n⌞M) by continuous fields with |γ| ≤ 1 supported near K (radial retraction and cutoff).
Mollify (|ω| ≤ 1 is preserved by convexity) to get admissible ω with T(ω) ≥ ∫_{M∩K} θ dH^n − ε.

subproblem.title: Locality of weighted approximate tangent spaces (Simon Ch. 3, 1.5(2), 1.8(1))
subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P open, M₁, M₂ ⊆ U null-measurable for H^n := μHE[n], and θ₁, θ₂ : ℝ^P → ℝ with θ_i > 0 on M_i and θ_i H^n-integrable on M_i ∩ K for every compact K ⊆ U (i = 1, 2). Then for H^n-a.e. x ∈ M₁ ∩ M₂ and every linear subspace Q ⊆ ℝ^P: if Q is the weighted approximate tangent space of M₁ with respect to θ₁ at x (HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M₁ θ₁ x Q, Simon Ch. 3, 1.7), then Q is also the weighted approximate tangent space of M₂ with respect to θ₂ at x.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Eucl P)), IsOpen U → ∀ (M₁ M₂ : Set (Eucl P)) (θ₁ θ₂ : Eucl P → ℝ), M₁ ⊆ U → M₂ ⊆ U → NullMeasurableSet M₁ (μHE[n] : Measure (Eucl P)) → NullMeasurableSet M₂ (μHE[n] : Measure (Eucl P)) → (∀ x ∈ M₁, 0 < θ₁ x) → (∀ x ∈ M₂, 0 < θ₂ x) → (∀ K : Set (Eucl P), IsCompact K → K ⊆ U → IntegrableOn θ₁ (M₁ ∩ K) (μHE[n] : Measure (Eucl P))) → (∀ K : Set (Eucl P), IsCompact K → K ⊆ U → IntegrableOn θ₂ (M₂ ∩ K) (μHE[n] : Measure (Eucl P))) → ∀ᵐ x ∂((μHE[n] : Measure (Eucl P)).restrict (M₁ ∩ M₂)), ∀ Q : Submodule ℝ (Eucl P), HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M₁ θ₁ x Q → HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M₂ θ₂ x Q
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Simon Ch. 3, Remark 1.5(2) and the proof of Theorem 1.6 “⇒”. There the approximate tangent space of M at x equals that of a piece M_j for H^n-a.e. x ∈ M_j, by the upper density theorem: the blow-up integrals over x + λ⁻¹(M ∖ M_j) tend to 0. Remark 1.8(1) gives the same for the weighted Definition 1.7. This is the tangent-space step of Simon's proof of 3.13 (“T_xM_C = T_xM_Q except for a set of small measure”), needed by the siblings im_series and localization. The density statements come from the Besicovitch differentiation theorem for the Radon measures θ_i H^n⌞M_i.

Notation. H := μHE[n], a positive finite multiple of μH[n]. For x ∈ ℝ^P and r > 0, η_{x,r}(y) := r⁻¹(y − x) (blowUpMap x r); B̄_r(x) is the closed ball; A := M₁ ∩ M₂. For i = 1, 2 let ν_i be the Borel measure ν_i(E) := ∫_{M_i∩E} θ_i dH. Recall that HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M θ x Q means: dim Q = n, and for every f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P), I^f_{M,θ}(r) := ∫_{η_{x,r}(M)} f(y)·θ(x + r y) dH(y) → θ(x)·∫_Q f dH as r → 0⁺.

1. (Blow-up change of variables.) Let x ∈ U, f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P) with spt f ⊆ B̄_R(0) (R > 0), and r > 0 with B̄_{Rr}(x) ⊆ U. Then for i = 1, 2
   I^f_{M_i,θ_i}(r) = r^{−n} ∫_{M_i} f((z − x)/r)·θ_i(z) dH(z),
   and both integrands are integrable. Indeed η_{x,r} is translation by −x followed by the dilation y ↦ r⁻¹y. H is translation invariant (IsometryEquiv.measurePreserving_euclideanHausdorffMeasure) and H(λE) = λⁿ H(E) for λ > 0 (euclideanHausdorffMeasure_smul₀). So (η_{x,r})_#(H⌞M_i) = rⁿ·H⌞η_{x,r}(M_i), i.e. ∫_{η_{x,r}(M_i)} h dH = r^{−n} ∫_{M_i} h∘η_{x,r} dH for nonnegative or integrable h; with h(y) := f(y)θ_i(x + ry) this is the identity. The right-hand integrand is bounded by sup|f|·θ_i·1_{M_i∩B̄_{Rr}(x)}, which is integrable because B̄_{Rr}(x) is a compact subset of U. Consequently, for every measurable E ⊆ ℝ^P,
   |r^{−n} ∫_{M_i∩E} f((z−x)/r) θ_i(z) dH(z)| ≤ sup|f| · r^{−n} ν_i(E ∩ B̄_{Rr}(x)).   (1)

2. (Localization of the measures.) Choose compact sets K_k ⊆ U (k ≥ 1) with U = ⋃_k interior(K_k), e.g. K_k := {x : |x| ≤ k, infDist(x, ℝ^P∖U) ≥ 1/k}, or K_k := B̄_k(0) if U = ℝ^P. Then ν_i^k := ν_i⌞K_k is a finite Borel measure (ν_i(K_k) = ∫_{M_i∩K_k} θ_i dH < ∞), hence locally finite. For x ∈ interior(K_k) and r < infDist(x, ℝ^P∖K_k) we have ν_i^k(E ∩ B̄_r(x)) = ν_i(E ∩ B̄_r(x)) for every E.

3. (Good points.) Fix k. Let g := θ₂/θ₁ on A and g := 0 off A. Then g is ν₁^k-integrable: ∫ |g| dν₁^k = ∫_{A∩K_k} θ₂ dH < ∞, since θ₂ = g θ₁ on A. Measurability follows from the a.e.-strong measurability of θ₁, θ₂ on M_i ∩ K_k and the null-measurability of A. Apply
   (a) the Besicovitch density theorem (Besicovitch.ae_tendsto_measure_inter_div) to ν₁^k and A, and to ν₂^k and A: for ν_i^k-a.e. x ∈ A, ν_i^k(A ∩ B̄_r(x)) / ν_i^k(B̄_r(x)) → 1 as r → 0⁺. In particular ν_i^k(B̄_r(x)) > 0 for small r, and ν_i^k(B̄_r(x) ∖ A) / ν_i^k(B̄_r(x)) → 0;
   (b) the Lebesgue differentiation theorem for the Besicovitch Vitali family of ν₁^k (VitaliFamily.ae_tendsto_lintegral_enorm_sub_div for Besicovitch.vitaliFamily ν₁^k, composed with Besicovitch.tendsto_filterAt to pass to closed balls B̄_r(x), r → 0⁺): for ν₁^k-a.e. x, (∫_{B̄_r(x)} |g − g(x)| dν₁^k) / ν₁^k(B̄_r(x)) → 0.
   A set N ⊆ A ∩ K_k with ν_i^k(N) = 0 is H-null: take a measurable N' ⊇ N with ν_i^k(N') = 0; then ∫_{N'∩M_i∩K_k} θ_i dH = 0 and θ_i > 0 on M_i, so H(N' ∩ M_i ∩ K_k) = 0. Hence the set G_k of points x ∈ A ∩ interior(K_k) at which (a) holds for i = 1, 2 and (b) holds has H-null complement in A ∩ interior(K_k). Put G := ⋃_k G_k. Since A ⊆ U = ⋃_k interior(K_k), A ∖ G is H-null.

4. (Main estimate.) Let x ∈ G, say x ∈ G_k, and let Q be a subspace with HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M₁ θ₁ x Q; then dim Q = n. Fix f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P) and R > 0 with spt f ⊆ B̄_R(0). For all small r > 0, B̄_{Rr}(x) ⊆ interior(K_k), so by step 2 ν_i may be replaced by ν_i^k on these balls. Put ε_i(r) := ν_i(B̄_{Rr}(x) ∖ A)/ν_i(B̄_{Rr}(x)) and λ(r) := (∫_{B̄_{Rr}(x)} |g − g(x)| dν₁)/ν₁(B̄_{Rr}(x)); both tend to 0 as r → 0⁺ by step 3.
   (i) Growth of ν₁. Let f₀(y) := max(0, min(1, R + 1 − |y|)); then f₀ ∈ C_c(ℝ^P), 0 ≤ f₀ ≤ 1 and f₀ = 1 on B̄_R(0). By step 1, r^{−n} ν₁(B̄_{Rr}(x)) ≤ I^{f₀}_{M₁,θ₁}(r) → θ₁(x) ∫_Q f₀ dH < ∞. Hence Λ₁ := limsup_{r→0⁺} r^{−n} ν₁(B̄_{Rr}(x)) < ∞.
   (ii) Growth of ν₂. ν₂(B̄_{Rr}(x) ∩ A) = ∫_{B̄_{Rr}(x)∩A} θ₂ dH = ∫_{B̄_{Rr}(x)} g dν₁ ≤ (g(x) + λ(r))·ν₁(B̄_{Rr}(x)), and ν₂(B̄_{Rr}(x)) = ν₂(B̄_{Rr}(x) ∩ A)/(1 − ε₂(r)) for small r. Hence limsup_{r→0⁺} r^{−n} ν₂(B̄_{Rr}(x)) ≤ g(x)·Λ₁ < ∞.
   (iii) Decomposition. By step 1, I^f_{M₂,θ₂}(r) = J₁(r) + J₂(r) with J₁(r) := r^{−n} ∫_A f((z−x)/r) θ₂(z) dH(z) and J₂(r) := r^{−n} ∫_{M₂∖A} f((z−x)/r) θ₂(z) dH(z).
   - By (1), |J₂(r)| ≤ sup|f|·r^{−n}ν₂(B̄_{Rr}(x))·ε₂(r) → 0, using (ii).
   - Since θ₂ = g θ₁ on A,
     J₁(r) = g(x)·r^{−n} ∫_A f((z−x)/r) θ₁ dH + r^{−n} ∫_A f((z−x)/r) (g(z) − g(x)) θ₁(z) dH(z).
     The second term is bounded by sup|f|·r^{−n}ν₁(B̄_{Rr}(x))·λ(r) → 0, using (i).
   - Further, r^{−n} ∫_A f((z−x)/r) θ₁ dH = I^f_{M₁,θ₁}(r) − r^{−n} ∫_{M₁∖A} f((z−x)/r) θ₁ dH. The last term is bounded by sup|f|·r^{−n}ν₁(B̄_{Rr}(x))·ε₁(r) → 0, using (i), and I^f_{M₁,θ₁}(r) → θ₁(x) ∫_Q f dH by hypothesis.
   (iv) Therefore I^f_{M₂,θ₂}(r) → g(x)·θ₁(x)·∫_Q f dH = θ₂(x)·∫_Q f dH (as x ∈ A, g(x)θ₁(x) = θ₂(x)). Since f was arbitrary and dim Q = n, HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M₂ θ₂ x Q.

5. (Conclusion.) Step 4 holds for every x ∈ G and every subspace Q, and (H⌞(M₁ ∩ M₂))-almost every x lies in G by step 3. This is the asserted ∀ᵐ statement. ∎
proof_key_steps: Blow-up change of variables I_i(r) = r^{−n}∫_{M_i} f((z−x)/r)θ_i(z) dH^n(z) (μHE translation invariance and dilation scaling).
Localize ν_i := θ_i H^n⌞M_i to compact sets K_k ⊂ U, where they are finite measures.
H^n-a.e. x ∈ M₁ ∩ M₂ is a Besicovitch density point of M₁ ∩ M₂ for ν₁ and ν₂ and a Lebesgue point of g := (θ₂/θ₁)·1_{M₁∩M₂} for ν₁; ν_i-null subsets are H^n-null because θ_i > 0.
The tangent hypothesis for (M₁, θ₁) gives r^{−n}ν₁(B̄_{Rr}(x)) = O(1), and then r^{−n}ν₂(B̄_{Rr}(x)) = O(1).
Split I₂(r) = g(x)·I₁(r) + o(1), so I₂(r) → θ₂(x)∫_Q f dH^n for every f ∈ C_c.

subproblem.title: M-absolutely convergent integer series of integer multiplicity currents (Simon 3.13)
subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P open, T_r ∈ D_n(U) (r ∈ ℕ) integer multiplicity currents and c_r ∈ ℤ such that Σ_r |c_r| M_W(T_r) < ∞ for every open W ⊂⊂ U. Then there is S ∈ D_n(U) such that for every ω ∈ D^n(U) the series Σ_r c_r T_r(ω) has (unconditional) sum S(ω), M_W(S) ≤ Σ_r |c_r| M_W(T_r) for every set W ⊆ ℝ^P, and S is integer multiplicity.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Eucl P)), IsOpen U → ∀ (T : ℕ → GeometricCurrentOn U n) (c : ℕ → ℤ), (∀ r, IsIntegerMultiplicity (T r)) → (∀ W, CompactlyContainedOpen W U → (∑' r, ((c r).natAbs : ℝ≥0∞) * (T r).massOn W) < ∞) → ∃ S : GeometricCurrentOn U n, (∀ ω, HasSum (fun r => (c r : ℝ) * T r ω) (S ω)) ∧ (∀ W, S.massOn W ≤ ∑' r, ((c r).natAbs : ℝ≥0∞) * (T r).massOn W) ∧ IsIntegerMultiplicity S
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Simon Ch. 6, Lemma 3.13 and its printed proof: the integer multiplicity currents are complete for the seminorms M_W; the multiplicities converge in L¹_loc(H^n) to an integer-valued function, the orientations converge, and “T_xM_C = T_xM_Q except for a set of small measure”. Here it is specialised to M-absolutely convergent integer series, which is how 3.13 is used for R^(ℓ), S^(ℓ) in the proof of 7.2; it contains Remark 3.2(1) (sibling im_lincomb). The tangent-space step is supplied by the sibling tangent_locality, and the identity M_W(τ(M,θ,ξ)) = ∫_{M∩W} θ dH^n (3.2(3)) by the sibling im_mass_formula.

Notation. H := μHE[n]; |α| := covectorEuclideanNorm α, a Euclidean norm on Λ^n; ‖ω‖ := sup_x |ω(x)| for a test form ω. For an open set W, W ⊂⊂ U means CompactlyContainedOpen W U.

(CB) (Cauchy–Binet bound; self-contained.) Let τ = (τ₁,…,τ_n) be orthonormal in ℝ^P and ζ := ±simpleNVector τ, so ζ(α) = ±α(τ₁,…,τ_n). Let A_{jk} := ⟨τ_j, e_k⟩ and, for strictly increasing I : Fin n → Fin P, let A_I be the n×n minor of A on the columns I. Let dx^I ∈ Λ^n be the covector with dx^I(e_J) = δ_{IJ} for increasing J, so α = Σ_I α(e_I) dx^I.
   (a) For every α ∈ Λ^n, α(τ) = Σ_I α(e_I) det A_I. Expand τ_j = Σ_k A_{jk} e_k by multilinearity; terms with a repeated basis vector vanish by alternation; group the remaining terms by their increasing rearrangement I, the sign of the sorting permutation producing det A_I.
   (b) Σ_I (det A_I)² = 1. Apply (a) to the alternating form α₀(v₁,…,v_n) := det(⟨τ_i, v_j⟩)_{i,j} (the wedge of the functionals ⟨τ_i, ·⟩), for which α₀(e_I) = det A_I and α₀(τ) = det(⟨τ_i, τ_j⟩) = 1.
   Consequences: by Cauchy–Schwarz in the coordinates (α(e_I))_I, |ζ(α)| ≤ |α| for every α ∈ Λ^n. The covector α^ζ := Σ_I ζ(dx^I) dx^I depends linearly on ζ and satisfies ζ(dx^I) = ±det A_I; hence |α^ζ| = 1 and ζ(α^ζ) = Σ_I (det A_I)² = 1. For n = 0 these claims are immediate (ζ(α) = ±α(), |α| = |α()|). For n > P there is no orthonormal n-frame.

1. (Mass bound.) For X ∈ D_k(U), any set V and η ∈ D^k(U) with tsupport η ⊆ V: ofReal |X(η)| ≤ M_V(X) · ofReal ‖η‖. If ‖η‖ = 0 then η = 0, since |·| is a norm. Otherwise ±η/‖η‖ is admissible for M_V(X), and GeometricCurrentOn.le_massOn applies.

2. (Definition of S.) Let ω ∈ D^n(U). Choose an open W ⊂⊂ U with tsupport ω ⊆ W, e.g. W := thickening(δ, tsupport ω) with cthickening(2δ, tsupport ω) ⊆ U. By step 1, Σ_r |c_r T_r(ω)| ≤ ‖ω‖ · Σ_r |c_r| M_W(T_r) < ∞; terms with c_r = 0 vanish, and if c_r ≠ 0 then M_W(T_r) < ∞. So (c_r T_r(ω))_r is absolutely summable in ℝ. Let S(ω) be its sum, so HasSum (fun r => c_r T_r(ω)) (S(ω)).

3. (S is a current.) S is linear, by HasSum.add, HasSum.mul_left and linearity of each T_r. For continuity, let ω_q → 0 in D^n(U) (TestFormOnConverges ω_q 0): all tsupport ω_q lie in one compact K ⊆ U, and all derivatives converge uniformly to 0 on K. Choose an open W ⊂⊂ U with K ⊆ W. Then |S(ω_q)| ≤ Σ_r |c_r| |T_r(ω_q)| ≤ ‖ω_q‖ · Σ_r |c_r| M_W(T_r) → 0. Here ‖ω_q‖ → 0 because ω_q → 0 uniformly on K, ω_q = 0 off K, and |·| is bounded by a constant times the operator norm on the finite-dimensional space Λ^n. Hence S is a GeometricCurrentOn U n.

4. (Mass bound for S.) Let V be any set and ω admissible for M_V(S) (tsupport ω ⊆ V, |ω| ≤ 1). By absolute summability and step 1 with ‖ω‖ ≤ 1, ofReal(S(ω)) ≤ Σ_r ofReal(|c_r| |T_r(ω)|) ≤ Σ_r |c_r| M_V(T_r). Taking the supremum gives M_V(S) ≤ Σ'_r |c_r| M_V(T_r).

5. (Representations; finiteness of overlaps.) Let I := {r : c_r ≠ 0}; indices outside I contribute nothing to S. For r ∈ I write T_r = τ(M_r, θ_r, ξ_r) with IsRectifiableTriple U n M_r θ_r ξ_r and θ_r(x) ∈ ℕ for x ∈ M_r; hence θ_r ≥ 1 on M_r. By the sibling im_mass_formula, M_W(T_r) = ∫_{M_r∩W} θ_r dH for open W. So for every W ⊂⊂ U:
   Σ_{r∈I} |c_r| ∫_{M_r∩W} θ_r dH < ∞.   (*)
   Let Θ := Σ_{r∈I} |c_r| θ_r 1_{M_r} : ℝ^P → [0, ∞]. By (*) and monotone convergence, Θ is H-integrable on every W ⊂⊂ U. Since U is a countable union of such W, N_∞ := {x ∈ U : Θ(x) = ∞} is H-null. A point x ∉ N_∞ lies in only finitely many M_r, r ∈ I, because each such r contributes |c_r| θ_r(x) ≥ 1 to Θ(x).

6. (Common tangent planes and orientations.)
   - For r ∈ I the orientation condition gives an H-null set N_r such that for x ∈ M_r ∖ N_r there is an orthonormal τ^r(x) with HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M_r θ_r x (span τ^r(x)) and ξ_r(x) = ±simpleNVector τ^r(x).
   - For r, r' ∈ I apply the sibling tangent_locality to (M₁, θ₁) := (M_r, θ_r) and (M₂, θ₂) := (M_{r'}, θ_{r'}); its hypotheses are part of the triple conditions. This gives an H-null set N_{r,r'} such that for x ∈ (M_r ∩ M_{r'}) ∖ N_{r,r'}, every weighted approximate tangent space of (M_r, θ_r) at x is also one of (M_{r'}, θ_{r'}) at x.
   - For x ∈ (M_r ∩ M_{r'}) ∖ (N_r ∪ N_{r'} ∪ N_{r,r'}), both span τ^r(x) and span τ^{r'}(x) are weighted approximate tangent spaces of (M_{r'}, θ_{r'}) at x. They coincide by HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt.unique, as θ_{r'}(x) ≠ 0.
   - Two orthonormal frames of the same n-dimensional subspace differ by an orthogonal matrix O, and simpleNVector(τ O) = det(O) · simpleNVector(τ) with det O = ±1 (multilinearity and alternation). Hence ξ_r(x) = ±ξ_{r'}(x).
   Let N₀ := N_∞ ∪ ⋃_r N_r ∪ ⋃_{r,r'} N_{r,r'}, an H-null set.

7. (Combined multiplicity and orientation.) Let M_∪ := ⋃_{r∈I} M_r. For x ∈ M_∪ ∖ N₀ let r(x) := min{r ∈ I : x ∈ M_r} and ξ̂(x) := ξ_{r(x)}(x). By step 6, for every r ∈ I with x ∈ M_r there is σ_r(x) ∈ {−1, 1} with ξ_r(x) = σ_r(x) ξ̂(x). Explicitly σ_r(x) = ξ_r(x)(β̂(x)), where β̂(x) := α^{ξ̂(x)} is the unit covector dual to ξ̂(x) given by (CB); so σ_r is a.e.-measurable. Define the integer θ̂(x) := Σ_{r∈I} c_r σ_r(x) θ_r(x) 1_{M_r}(x), a finite sum by step 5, and
   M_S := {x ∈ M_∪ ∖ N₀ : θ̂(x) ≠ 0},  θ_S := |θ̂| on M_S (0 elsewhere),  ξ_S := sign(θ̂) ξ̂ on M_S (0 elsewhere).
   No modification is made: these objects are defined pointwise. Off N_∞, θ̂ is a pointwise finite sum of countably many H-a.e.-measurable terms, so θ̂ is H⌞M_∪-a.e. measurable. Hence M_S is H-null-measurable, and θ_S, ξ_S are H⌞M_S-a.e. strongly measurable; r(x) and the indicators 1_{M_r} are built from countably many null-measurable sets.

8. (S = τ(M_S, θ_S, ξ_S).) Let ω ∈ D^n(U) and W ⊂⊂ U open with tsupport ω ⊆ W. Since |ξ_r(x)(α)| ≤ |α| a.e. on M_r by (CB),
Σ_{r∈I} ∫ |c_r θ_r 1_{M_r} ξ_r(ω)| dH ≤ ‖ω‖ Σ_r |c_r| ∫_{M_r∩W} θ_r dH < ∞.
So the series may be integrated term by term (integral_tsum, or dominated convergence for the partial sums):

subproblem.title: Flat-Cauchy subsequence summed to the weak limit (Simon 7.2 proof, (5) and 3.13)
subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P open and T_j, T ∈ D_n(U). Assume (total boundedness) that for every ε ∈ (0, ∞] and every infinite J ⊆ ℕ there is an infinite J' ⊆ J such that for all i, j ∈ J' there are integer multiplicity R ∈ D_{n+1}(U), S ∈ D_n(U) with T_i − T_j = ∂R + S and M(R) + M(S) < ε (M = M_U), and assume T_j ⇀ T. Then there is a strictly increasing φ : ℕ → ℕ such that for every ℓ ∈ ℕ there are integer multiplicity R ∈ D_{n+1}(U), S ∈ D_n(U) with T_{φ(ℓ)} − T = ∂R + S and M(R) + M(S) ≤ 2·2^{−ℓ}.

Source: Simon Ch. 6, proof of 7.2.

- The last paragraph: “by 3.13 we can define integer multiplicity R^(ℓ), S^(ℓ) by the M-absolutely convergent series … M(R^(ℓ)) + M(S^(ℓ)) ≤ 2^{−ℓ+1} and (from (5)) T − T_{j_ℓ} = ∂R^(ℓ) + S^(ℓ)”.
This is Steps 6–7 of the parent proof. The Lean sign convention (T_{j_ℓ} − T = ∂R + S) is obtained directly by using the pairwise decompositions in the order T_{j_r} − T_{j_{r+1}}; the hypothesis provides both orders, so no negation is needed. M denotes the global mass on U (GeometricCurrentOn.mass = massOn U).

1. (Nested index sets.) Define infinite sets J_0 := ℕ ⊇ J_1 ⊇ J_2 ⊇ … recursively: J_{r+1} is a set J' given by the hypothesis for ε := 2^{−r} (> 0) and J := J_r (infinite). Thus J_{r+1} ⊆ J_r is infinite, and for all i, j ∈ J_{r+1} there are integer multiplicity R ∈ D_{n+1}(U), S ∈ D_n(U) with T_i − T_j = ∂R + S and M(R) + M(S) < 2^{−r}.

2. (Indices; printed (5).) Choose j_0 ∈ J_1 and, recursively, j_{r+1} ∈ J_{r+2} with j_{r+1} > j_r; this is possible since J_{r+2} is infinite. Put φ(r) := j_r; φ is strictly increasing and j_r ∈ J_{r+1} for all r. Since J_{r+2} ⊆ J_{r+1}, both j_r and j_{r+1} lie in J_{r+1}. So by step 1 there are integer multiplicity R_r ∈ D_{n+1}(U), S_r ∈ D_n(U) with T_{j_r}(ω) − T_{j_{r+1}}(ω) = ∂R_r(ω) + S_r(ω) for all ω ∈ D^n(U) and M(R_r) + M(S_r) < 2^{−r}.

3. (The series R^(ℓ), S^(ℓ); 3.13.) Fix ℓ ∈ ℕ. Apply the sibling im_series to the sequence (R_{ℓ+k})_{k∈ℕ} with c_k := 1. Its hypothesis holds because, for every open W ⊂⊂ U, Σ_k M_W(R_{ℓ+k}) ≤ Σ_k M(R_{ℓ+k}) ≤ Σ_k 2^{−(ℓ+k)} < ∞ (massOn_mono, W ⊆ U). This gives an integer multiplicity R^(ℓ) ∈ D_{n+1}(U) with HasSum (fun k => R_{ℓ+k}(η)) (R^(ℓ)(η)) for every η ∈ D^{n+1}(U), and M(R^(ℓ)) ≤ Σ_k M(R_{ℓ+k}) (its mass bound with W := U). Likewise we get an integer multiplicity S^(ℓ) ∈ D_n(U) from (S_{ℓ+k})_k, with HasSum (fun k => S_{ℓ+k}(ω)) (S^(ℓ)(ω)) and M(S^(ℓ)) ≤ Σ_k M(S_{ℓ+k}).

4. (Identification of the limit.) Let ω ∈ D^n(U); write dω = exteriorDerivativeTestOn U n ω, so ∂R(ω) = R(dω). Telescoping step 2 gives, for every N,
T_{j_ℓ}(ω) − T_{j_{ℓ+N}}(ω) = Σ_{k<N} (T_{j_{ℓ+k}}(ω) − T_{j_{ℓ+k+1}}(ω)) = Σ_{k<N} (R_{ℓ+k}(dω) + S_{ℓ+k}(ω)).
As N → ∞:
   - the right-hand side tends to R^(ℓ)(dω) + S^(ℓ)(ω) (HasSum.tendsto_sum_nat at the forms dω and ω);
   - the left-hand side tends to T_{j_ℓ}(ω) − T(ω), because j_{ℓ+N} → ∞ and T_j(ω) → T(ω) (WeaklyConvergesOn Tj T).
Hence T_{φ(ℓ)}(ω) − T(ω) = ∂R^(ℓ)(ω) + S^(ℓ)(ω) for all ω.

5. (Mass.) Using ENNReal.tsum_add and the geometric series in [0, ∞],
M(R^(ℓ)) + M(S^(ℓ)) ≤ Σ_k M(R_{ℓ+k}) + Σ_k M(S_{ℓ+k}) = Σ_k (M(R_{ℓ+k}) + M(S_{ℓ+k})) ≤ Σ_k 2^{−(ℓ+k)} = 2 · 2^{−ℓ}.

6. (Conclusion.) φ is strictly increasing and, for each ℓ, R := R^(ℓ) and S := S^(ℓ) are integer multiplicity with T_{φ(ℓ)} − T = ∂R + S and M(R) + M(S) ≤ 2 · 2^{−ℓ}. ∎

subproblem.title: Integer linear combinations of integer multiplicity currents (Simon 3.2(1))
subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P open, T₁, T₂ ∈ D_n(U) integer multiplicity, a, b ∈ ℤ, and S ∈ D_n(U) with S(ω) = a·T₁(ω) + b·T₂(ω) for every ω ∈ D^n(U). Then S is integer multiplicity.

subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Simon Ch. 6, Remark 3.2(1): if T₁, T₂ are integer multiplicity then so is p₁T₁ + p₂T₂ for p₁, p₂ ∈ ℤ. It is obtained here as the finite case of the series lemma (sibling im_series); this is the parent's preliminary (P2).

1. (Local finiteness of mass.) Let X ∈ D_n(U) be integer multiplicity, X = τ(M, θ, ξ) with IsRectifiableTriple U n M θ ξ, and let W ⊂⊂ U be open (CompactlyContainedOpen W U). By the sibling im_mass_formula (W is open), M_W(X) = ∫⁻_{M∩W} ofReal θ dH ≤ ∫⁻_{M∩closure W} ofReal θ dH < ∞. The last bound holds because closure W is a compact subset of U and θ is integrable on M ∩ closure W (integrableOn condition; IntegrableOn.lintegral_lt_top).

2. (A two-term series.) Define T_r := T₂ if r = 1 and T_r := T₁ otherwise, and c₀ := a, c₁ := b, c_r := 0 for r ≥ 2. Every T_r is integer multiplicity. For every open W ⊂⊂ U, Σ'_r |c_r| M_W(T_r) = |a| M_W(T₁) + |b| M_W(T₂) < ∞ by step 1, since the family vanishes outside {0, 1} (tsum_eq_sum).

3. (Apply im_series.) The sibling im_series gives an integer multiplicity S' ∈ D_n(U) with HasSum (fun r => c_r T_r(ω)) (S'(ω)) for every ω. The family has finite support {0, 1}, so it also has sum a T₁(ω) + b T₂(ω) (hasSum_sum_of_ne_finset_zero). By uniqueness of sums, S'(ω) = a T₁(ω) + b T₂(ω) = S(ω).

4. (Conclusion.) S' and S agree on every test form, so S' = S (GeometricCurrentOn.ext), and S is integer multiplicity. ∎

Apply im_series to the family (T₁, T₂, T₁, T₁, …) with coefficients (a, b, 0, 0, …).
The resulting current equals S on every test form (finite-support HasSum, uniqueness of sums, ext), so S is integer multiplicity.

Let A_{jl} := ⟨τ_j, e_l⟩ and, for strictly increasing I : Fin k → Fin P, let A_I be the k×k minor of A on the columns I. Let dx^I ∈ Λ^k be the covector with dx^I(e_J) = δ_{IJ} for increasing J, so α = Σ_I α(e_I) dx^I.
   (a) For every α ∈ Λ^k, α(τ) = Σ_I α(e_I) det A_I. Expand τ_j = Σ_l A_{jl} e_l by multilinearity; terms with a repeated basis vector vanish by alternation; group the remaining terms by their increasing rearrangement I, the sign of the sorting permutation producing det A_I.
   (b) Σ_I (det A_I)² = 1. Apply (a) to the alternating form α₀(v₁,…,v_k) := det(⟨τ_i, v_j⟩)_{i,j}, for which α₀(e_I) = det A_I and α₀(τ) = det(⟨τ_i, τ_j⟩) = 1.
   Consequently, by Cauchy–Schwarz in the coordinates (α(e_I))_I, |ζ(α)| ≤ |α| for every α ∈ Λ^k; in particular |ζ(dx^I)| ≤ 1. For k = 0 this is immediate (ζ(α) = ±α(), |α| = |α()|).
(F1) The zero current is integer multiplicity: take M = ∅, so every condition of IsRectifiableTriple is vacuous and the integral over ∅ is 0. Also ∂0 = 0, M_V(0) = 0 for every V, and spt 0 = ∅ (every x ∈ U has a ball with compact closure in U on which 0 vanishes). M_∅(X) = 0 for every current X, since the only form with tsupport ⊆ ∅ is 0.
(F2) For X, Y ∈ D_k(U) and a, b ∈ ℤ, the map ω ↦ aX(ω) + bY(ω) is linear and sequentially continuous, hence a current, with boundary a∂X + b∂Y. If X and Y are integer multiplicity, so is aX + bY (sibling im_lincomb). For every set V: M_V(X + Y) ≤ M_V(X) + M_V(Y), since ofReal(s + t) ≤ ofReal s + ofReal t; and M_V(−X) = M_V(X), since ω is admissible iff −ω is.
(F3) Mass bound: ofReal |X(η)| ≤ M_V(X) · ofReal ‖η‖ whenever tsupport η ⊆ V. Apply GeometricCurrentOn.le_massOn to ±η/‖η‖; if ‖η‖ = 0 then η = 0.
(F4) Mass formula (sibling im_mass_formula): if X(ω) = ∫_M θ ξ(ω) dH for a rectifiable triple (M, θ, ξ) in U, then M_V(X) = ∫_{M∩V} θ dH for every open V. For an integer multiplicity X = τ(M_X, θ_X, ξ_X) write μ_X(E) := ∫_{M_X∩E} θ_X dH; then μ_X(V) = M_V(X) < ∞ for V ⊂⊂ U. Also |ξ_X(x)(α)| ≤ |α| for H-a.e. x ∈ M_X, because ξ_X(x) = ±simpleNVector of an orthonormal frame by the orientation condition (F0).
(F5) Restriction formula (uniqueness of the representing vector measure). Let X ∈ D_k(U) with X(ω) = ∫_M θ ξ(ω) dH for a rectifiable triple (M, θ, ξ), let A ⊆ ℝ^P be Borel, and let Y ∈ D_k(U) with IsRestriction X A Y, i.e. Y(ω) = ∫_A v(x)(ω(x)) dμ(x) for some (μ, v) with IsMeasureRepresentation X μ v. Then Y(ω) = ∫_{M∩A} θ ξ(ω) dH for all ω ∈ D^k(U).
   Proof.
   (i) Put v_I(x) := v(x)(dx^I), ξ_I(x) := ξ(x)(dx^I) and ω_I(x) := ω(x)(e_I). Then v(x)(ω(x)) = Σ_I ω_I(x) v_I(x) and ξ(x)(ω(x)) = Σ_I ω_I(x) ξ_I(x).
   (ii) Let O be open with closure O compact ⊆ U, and φ_O ∈ C_c^∞(U) with 0 ≤ φ_O ≤ 1 and φ_O = 1 on closure O. Testing the representation with φ_O dx^I ∈ D^k(U) shows that v_I is μ-integrable on O. Also θ ξ_I is H-integrable on M ∩ O, since |ξ_I| ≤ 1 a.e. on M (F0) and θ is integrable on M ∩ closure O. So λ_I(E) := ∫_{E∩O} v_I dμ and λ'_I(E) := ∫_{E∩O∩M} θ ξ_I dH (E ⊆ ℝ^P Borel) are finite signed Borel measures on ℝ^P concentrated on O, and ∫ ψ dλ_I = X(ψ dx^I) = ∫ ψ dλ'_I for every ψ ∈ C_c^∞(O).
   (iii) Every ψ ∈ C_c(O) is the uniform limit of its mollifications, which are uniformly bounded with supports in a fixed compact subset of O; so ∫ ψ dλ_I = ∫ ψ dλ'_I for ψ ∈ C_c(O) by dominated convergence. For a compact C ⊆ O, 1_C is the decreasing limit of ψ_q(x) := max(0, 1 − q·dist(x, C)), which lie in C_c(O) for q large (dist(C, ℝ^P ∖ O) > 0); so λ_I(C) = λ'_I(C). Let K_q be compact sets increasing to O. For a closed F ⊆ ℝ^P the compact sets F ∩ K_q increase to F ∩ O, so λ_I(F) = lim_q λ_I(F ∩ K_q) = lim_q λ'_I(F ∩ K_q) = λ'_I(F), both measures being concentrated on O. The closed sets form a π-system generating the Borel σ-algebra of ℝ^P. So the finite positive measures ν₁ := v_I⁺·μ⌞O + (θξ_I)⁻·H⌞(M ∩ O) and ν₂ := (θξ_I)⁺·H⌞(M ∩ O) + v_I⁻·μ⌞O, which agree on closed sets (including ℝ^P), are equal (MeasureTheory.ext_of_generate_finite). Hence λ_I = λ'_I.
   (iv) Given ω, choose O as in (ii) with tsupport ω ⊆ O. Each ω_I is bounded, Borel and vanishes off tsupport ω, so Y(ω) = Σ_I ∫ 1_A ω_I dλ_I = Σ_I ∫ 1_A ω_I dλ'_I = ∫_{M∩A} θ ξ(ω) dH. Points outside U contribute nothing to either side, since ω = 0 there. ∎
(F6) Restrictions of integer multiplicity currents. Let X = τ(M, θ, ξ) be integer multiplicity in U and A Borel. Then (M ∩ A, θ, ξ) is an integer multiplicity rectifiable triple in U:
   - M ∩ A ⊆ U is null-measurable and countably n-rectifiable (CountablyRectifiable.mono);
   - θ ∈ ℕ and θ > 0 on M ∩ A, and θ is integrable on M ∩ A ∩ K for compact K ⊆ U;
   - ξ is measurable for H⌞(M ∩ A);
   - orientation: apply the sibling tangent_locality to (M₁, θ₁) := (M, θ) and (M₂, θ₂) := (M ∩ A, θ). For H-a.e. x ∈ M ∩ A, the weighted approximate tangent space span τ(x) of (M, θ) at x (given by the orientation condition of X) is also that of (M ∩ A, θ), and ξ(x) = ±simpleNVector τ(x).
   The functional X⌞A(ω) := ∫_{M∩A} θ ξ(ω) dH is linear and satisfies |X⌞A(ω)| ≤ ‖ω‖ μ_X(K) when tsupport ω ⊆ K, hence is sequentially continuous. So X⌞A is a current, and it is integer multiplicity. IsRestriction X A (X⌞A) holds with the representation μ := H⌞M (μHE[n].restrict M) and v := θ • ξ: for each ω, x ↦ v(x)(ω(x)) = θ(x) ξ(x)(ω(x)) is μ-integrable (bounded by ‖ω‖ θ 1_{M∩tsupport ω}, F0), ∫ v(ω) dμ = tauAction n M θ ξ ω = X(ω), and ∫_A v(ω) dμ = X⌞A(ω). By F5, every Y with IsRestriction X A Y equals X⌞A; in particular it is integer multiplicity. By F4, M_V(X⌞A) = μ_X(V ∩ A) for open V.

Main proof.
1. (Trivial cases.) Suppose W = ∅, or every (m+1)-covector on ℝ^P vanishes (this happens exactly when P < m + 1, e.g. P = 0). Take ψ := id, K := ∅, B := 0, T' := 0 and T'_j := 0. All assertions except the last hold by F1. For the last one, R₀ := 0 and S₀ := T_j − T (integer multiplicity by F2) satisfy T_j − T = ∂R₀ + S₀, so flatDistance W (T_j) T ≤ M_W(S₀) + M_W(R₀). If W = ∅ this is 0 (F1). If P < m + 1, all currents of degree m + 1 vanish, so S₀ = 0 and it is again 0. Hence flatDistance W (T_j) T ≤ M_W(S) + M_W(R) for all R, S. From now on W ≠ ∅ and P ≥ m + 1 ≥ 1.
2. (Level function.) closure W is compact and ⊆ U, so there is δ > 0 with cthickening(2δ, closure W) ⊆ U. Let W' := thickening(δ, closure W). Then W' is open and bounded, closure W' ⊆ cthickening(δ, closure W) is compact and ⊆ U, so W' ⊂⊂ U, and closure W ⊆ W'. As W' is bounded and P ≥ 1, ℝ^P ∖ W' ≠ ∅. Let φ(x) := infDist(x, ℝ^P ∖ W'); φ is 1-Lipschitz on ℝ^P, and φ(x) > 0 iff x ∈ W' (W' is open). Let 2r₀ := min_{closure W} φ > 0, a := r₀/2 and b := r₀. For t > 0 put A_t := {x : φ(x) ≥ t}. A_t is closed, contained in W' ⊆ U (so A_t = {x ∈ U : φ(x) ≥ t}) and bounded, hence compact; and closure W ⊆ {φ > t} ⊆ A_t for t < 2r₀. Put B' := B_{W'} < ∞.
3. (Representations.) Write T_j = τ(M_j, θ_j, ξ_j) and T = τ(M_T, θ_T, ξ_T). For every V ⊂⊂ U, M_V(∂T_j) ≤ B_V < ∞, so ∂T_j is integer multiplicity by BoundaryRectifiability: ∂T_j = τ(M'_j, θ'_j, ξ'_j). Let μ_j := μ_{T_j}, μ'_j := μ_{∂T_j} and μ_T as in F4. Then μ_j(W') = M_{W'}(T_j) ≤ B', μ'_j(W') ≤ B' and μ_T(W') = M_{W'}(T) < ∞.
4. (Helly-type selection; parent Step 4(i).) For t > 0 let F_j(t) := μ_j(A_t) ∈ [0, B'] (A_t ⊆ W'); each F_j is nonincreasing. Enumerate the positive rationals. By Bolzano–Weierstrass and Cantor's diagonal argument there is a strictly increasing ψ₁ : ℕ → ℕ such that G(q) := lim_j F_{ψ₁(j)}(q) exists for every rational q > 0; G is nonincreasing on ℚ_{>0}. For t > 0 let G₋(t) := inf{G(q) : q ∈ ℚ, 0 < q < t} and G₊(t) := sup{G(q) : q ∈ ℚ, q > t}; then G₊(t) ≤ G₋(t). The set D := {t > 0 : G₊(t) < G₋(t)} is countable: for t < t' in D, G₋(t') ≤ G(q) ≤ G₊(t) for a rational q ∈ (t, t'), so the nonempty open intervals (G₊(t), G₋(t)), t ∈ D, are pairwise disjoint and each contains a rational.
5. (Slices and Fatou; parent Step 4(ii).) For each j apply SlicingTheorem to T_{ψ₁(j)}, with f := φ and L := 1 (LipschitzOnWith 1 φ U). Its hypothesis holds: M_V(T_{ψ₁(j)}) < ∞ and M_V(∂T_{ψ₁(j)}) < ∞ for V ⊂⊂ U. This gives slices S^j_t ∈ D_m(U) with IsSlice T_{ψ₁(j)} φ t (S^j_t) for every t ∈ ℝ. Apply its last clause with:
   - the open set U ⊆ U in place of W;
   - L_W := 1 (for every x, ‖fderiv ℝ φ x‖₊ ≤ 1: at points of differentiability by the Lipschitz bound, and fderiv = 0 elsewhere);
   - the interval (a, b);
   - R := T_{ψ₁(j)}⌞{x ∈ U : a < φ(x) < b}, for which IsRestriction holds by F6.
   This gives a measurable g_j : ℝ → [0, ∞] with M_U(S^j_t) ≤ g_j(t) for t ∈ (a, b) and ∫⁻_{(a,b)} g_j ≤ 1 · M_U(R) = μ_{ψ₁(j)}({a < φ < b}) ≤ μ_{ψ₁(j)}(W') ≤ B' (F6, F4; {φ > a} ⊆ W'). By Fatou's lemma (lintegral_liminf_le), ∫⁻_{(a,b)} liminf_j g_j ≤ liminf_j ∫⁻_{(a,b)} g_j ≤ B' < ∞. So liminf_j g_j(t) < ∞ for Lebesgue-a.e. t ∈ (a, b).
6. (Choice of the level; parent Step 4(iii).) The set of t ∈ (a, b) with t ∉ D and liminf_j g_j(t) < ∞ has full measure in (a, b) (D is countable), hence is nonempty; fix such an s. Let L_s := liminf_j g_j(s) < ∞. The set {j : g_j(s) < L_s + 1} is infinite, so there is a strictly increasing ψ₂ with g_{ψ₂(k)}(s) ≤ L_s + 1 for all k. Put ψ := ψ₁ ∘ ψ₂ (strictly increasing) and, for k ∈ ℕ, T*_k := T_{ψ(k)} and S_k := S^{ψ₂(k)}_s. Write M*_k, θ*_k, ξ*_k, μ*_k, μ'*_k for the data of T*_k and ∂T*_k. Then F_{ψ(k)}(q) → G(q) for every rational q > 0, and G₊(s) = G₋(s). Set K := A_s (compact, ⊆ U) and B := 2B' + L_s + 1 < ∞.
7. (Localized currents.) Let E_s := {x ∈ U : φ(x) < s} (Borel) and note U ∖ E_s = A_s. By IsSlice T*_k φ s S_k there are A_k ∈ D_n(U), B_k ∈ D_m(U) with IsRestriction T*_k E_s A_k, IsRestriction (∂T*_k) E_s B_k, and S_k(ω) = ∂A_k(ω) − B_k(ω) for all ω. By F5 (with the representations of step 3), A_k = T*_k⌞E_s and B_k = (∂T*_k)⌞E_s. Define T'_k := T*_k − A_k (a current by F2) and T' := T⌞A_s (F6). Since M*_k ⊆ U, T'_k(ω) = ∫_{M*_k∩A_s} θ*_k ξ*_k(ω) dH, i.e. T'_k = T*_k⌞A_s.
   (a) T'_k and T' are integer multiplicity (F6).
   (b) ∂T'_k = ∂T*_k − ∂A_k = (∂T*_k − B_k) − S_k, and ∂T*_k − B_k = (∂T*_k)⌞A_s (F5, and F6 for the integer multiplicity current ∂T*_k).
   (c) Masses: M(T'_k) = μ*_k(A_s) ≤ μ*_k(W') ≤ B' (F6, F4). Also M(∂T'_k) ≤ M((∂T*_k)⌞A_s) + M(S_k) ≤ μ'*_k(W') + g_{ψ₂(k)}(s) ≤ B' + L_s + 1, by F2, F6, step 5 with s ∈ (a, b), and step 6. Hence M(T'_k) + M(∂T'_k) ≤ B.
   (d) ∂T'_k is integer multiplicity, by BoundaryRectifiability applied to T'_k: M_V(∂T'_k) ≤ M(∂T'_k) < ∞ for V ⊂⊂ U, by massOn_mono.
   (e) spt T'_k ⊆ K: let x ∈ U ∖ A_s. Then x ∈ E_s, which is open, so there is ρ > 0 such that the ball B_ρ(x) has compact closure contained in E_s. Every ω with tsupport ω ⊆ B_ρ(x) vanishes on A_s, so T'_k(ω) = 0. Thus B_ρ(x) lies in zeroRegion(T'_k) and x ∉ spt T'_k.
8. (Weak convergence T'_k ⇀ T'; parent Step 4(iv).) Fix ω ∈ D^n(U) and ε > 0.
   - Choose rationals q₂ > s and q₁ ∈ (a, s) with G(q₁) − G(q₂) < ε and μ_T({q₁ < φ < s}) < ε. This is possible: G(q) → G₋(s) as q ↑ s and G(q) → G₊(s) = G₋(s) as q ↓ s through rationals; and μ_T({q < φ < s}) → 0 as q ↑ s by continuity from above of the finite measure μ_T⌞W', the sets decreasing to ∅.
   - Let χ : ℝ^P → [0, 1] be smooth with χ = 1 on {φ ≥ s} and χ = 0 on {φ ≤ q₁} (smooth Urysohn lemma for these disjoint closed sets, exists_contMDiffMap_zero_one_of_isClosed). Then χω ∈ D^n(U) and, on U, |1_{A_s} − χ| ≤ 1_{q₁ < φ < s}.
   - Using F0 and F4 (|ξ*_k(x)(ω(x))| ≤ ‖ω‖ for H-a.e. x ∈ M*_k):
     |T'_k(ω) − T*_k(χω)| = |∫_{M*_k} θ*_k (1_{A_s} − χ) ξ*_k(ω) dH| ≤ ‖ω‖ μ*_k({q₁ < φ < s}) ≤ ‖ω‖ (F_{ψ(k)}(q₁) − F_{ψ(k)}(q₂)),
     because {q₁ < φ < s} ⊆ A_{q₁} ∖ A_{q₂} and μ*_k(A_{q₂}) ≤ μ*_k(A_{q₁}) < ∞. Likewise |T'(ω) − T(χω)| ≤ ‖ω‖ μ_T({q₁ < φ < s}) ≤ ε ‖ω‖.
   - Since (T*_k) is a subsequence of (T_j) and T_j ⇀ T, T*_k(χω) → T(χω).
   Hence limsup_k |T'_k(ω) − T'(ω)| ≤ ‖ω‖ (G(q₁) − G(q₂)) + ε ‖ω‖ ≤ 2ε ‖ω‖. As ε > 0 is arbitrary, T'_k(ω) → T'(ω); thus WeaklyConvergesOn T'_k T'.
9. (Transfer; parent Step 4(v).) Let k ∈ ℕ, and let R ∈ D_{n+1}(U), S ∈ D_n(U) be integer multiplicity with T'_k(ω) − T'(ω) = ∂R(ω) + S(ω) for all ω. Put Z*_k := T*_k − T'_k = A_k = T*_k⌞E_s and Z := T − T' = T⌞E_s (as M_T ⊆ U); both are integer multiplicity (F6). Let Ŝ := S + Z*_k − Z, integer multiplicity by F2 applied twice. Then for all ω,
T*_k(ω) − T(ω) = (T'_k(ω) − T'(ω)) + Z*_k(ω) − Z(ω) = ∂R(ω) + Ŝ(ω).
So (R, Ŝ) is admissible in the infimum defining flatDistance W (T_{ψ(k)}) T, whence flatDistance W (T_{ψ(k)}) T ≤ M_W(Ŝ) + M_W(R). If tsupport ω ⊆ W, then ω = 0 on E_s (as W ⊆ {φ ≥ 2r₀} and s < 2r₀), so Z*_k(ω) = Z(ω) = 0 and Ŝ(ω) = S(ω). Therefore M_W(Ŝ) = M_W(S), and flatDistance W (T_{ψ(k)}) T ≤ M_W(S) + M_W(R).
10. (Conclusion.) By steps 6–9: ψ is strictly increasing; K is compact with K ⊆ U; B ≠ ∞; every T'_k and ∂T'_k is integer multiplicity; spt T'_k ⊆ K; M(T'_k) + M(∂T'_k) ≤ B; T'_k ⇀ T'; and the transfer inequality holds. ∎

W' := thickening of closure W, φ := infDist(·, ℝ^P ∖ W'), A_t := {φ ≥ t} compact; restriction calculus: any IsRestriction of τ(M, θ, ξ) to A equals τ(M ∩ A, θ, ξ) (uniqueness of the representing vector measure) and is integer multiplicity (tangent_locality).
Diagonal subsequence along which μ_{T_j}(A_q) converges for all rational q; the limit G has countably many jumps.

Slicing (4.10 clause with W := U, L_W := 1) and Fatou give liminf_j M(slice_j(t)) < ∞ for a.e. t; choose a level s that is also a continuity point of G, and a further subsequence with bounded slice masses.
T'_j := T_{ψ(j)}⌞A_s is integer multiplicity; ∂T'_j = (∂T_{ψ(j)})⌞A_s − slice is integer multiplicity by BoundaryRectifiability; spt T'_j ⊆ A_s; uniform mass bound B.
T'_j ⇀ T⌞A_s via smooth cutoffs between rational levels q₁ < s < q₂ and continuity of G at s.
Transfer: T_{ψ(j)} − T = ∂R + (S + Z_j − Z), with Z_j, Z the integer multiplicity restrictions to {φ < s}, which vanish on forms supported in W.

subproblem.title: Total boundedness of compactly supported integral currents (Simon 7.2 proof, (1)–(3))
subproblem.statement: Assume the Deformation Theorem (DeformationTheorem). Let P, m ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P open, K ⊆ U compact, B ∈ [0, ∞), and T_j ∈ D_{m+1}(U) (j ∈ ℕ) integer multiplicity with ∂T_j integer multiplicity, spt T_j ⊆ K and M(T_j) + M(∂T_j) ≤ B for all j (M = M_U). Then for every ε ∈ (0, ∞] and every infinite J ⊆ ℕ there is an infinite J' ⊆ J such that for all i, j ∈ J' there are integer multiplicity R ∈ D_{m+2}(U), S ∈ D_{m+1}(U) with T_i − T_j = ∂R + S and M(R) + M(S) < ε.

subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Simon Ch. 6, proof of 7.2, (1)–(3): “the main difficulty is to establish the appropriate total boundedness property … an easy consequence of the Deformation Theorem: … 5.3 guarantees that for T ∈ I_{M,W} we can find integer multiplicity P, R, S with (2), (3) … since there are only finitely many currents P as in (2), we have (1)”. It is used in the pigeonhole form of the parent proof's Step 5, with the preliminaries (P3) extension/restriction of domains, (P4) lattice chains and (P5) approximation with control.

Notation. n := m + 1; H := μHE[n]; |α| := covectorEuclideanNorm α; ‖ω‖ := sup_x |ω(x)|. M := M_U for currents on U and M := M_{ℝ^P} for currents on ℝ^P (GeometricCurrentOn.mass). “aX + bY” is the current ω ↦ aX(ω) + bY(ω).

0. (P < n.) Every alternating map of degree > P on ℝ^P vanishes, so every test form of degree n or n + 1 is 0 and every current of degree n or n + 1 is the zero current. Take J' := J and, for i, j ∈ J', R := 0 and S := 0 (integer multiplicity by F1). Then T_i − T_j = 0 = ∂0 + 0 and M(0) + M(0) = 0 < ε. From now on P ≥ n.

Preliminary facts.
(F1)–(F3)
   - The zero current is integer multiplicity with zero mass.
   - aX + bY is a current with ∂(aX + bY) = a∂X + b∂Y; it is integer multiplicity when X, Y are and a, b ∈ ℤ (sibling im_lincomb).
   - M_V(X + Y) ≤ M_V(X) + M_V(Y) and M_V(−X) = M_V(X).
   - ofReal |X(η)| ≤ M_V(X) · ofReal ‖η‖ when tsupport η ⊆ V (rescale ±η/‖η‖ and use GeometricCurrentOn.le_massOn).
(F4) Mass formula (sibling im_mass_formula): M_V(τ(M, θ, ξ)) = ∫_{M∩V} θ dH for open V, for every rectifiable triple (M, θ, ξ).
(G1) Support vanishing. If X ∈ D_k(U), η ∈ D^k(U) and tsupport η ∩ spt X = ∅, then X(η) = 0.
   Proof: tsupport η is a compact subset of zeroRegion(X) = ⋃{V open : closure V compact ⊆ U, X vanishes on V}. Choose finitely many such V_1, …, V_N covering tsupport η, and a smooth partition of unity ψ_1, …, ψ_N with tsupport ψ_i ⊆ V_i and Σ_i ψ_i = 1 on tsupport η (SmoothPartitionOfUnity subordinate to the cover). Then η = Σ_i ψ_i η with tsupport(ψ_i η) ⊆ V_i, so X(η) = Σ_i X(ψ_i η) = 0.
   In particular spt ∂X ⊆ spt X, since ∂X(η) = X(dη) and tsupport dη ⊆ tsupport η.
(G2) Let X = τ(M, θ, ξ) be integer multiplicity in U. Then H(M ∖ spt X) = 0, X = τ(M ∩ spt X, θ, ξ), and (M ∩ spt X, θ, ξ) is again an integer multiplicity rectifiable triple.
   Proof: V := U ∖ spt X = zeroRegion(X) is open, and X(η) = 0 whenever tsupport η ⊆ V (G1), so M_V(X) = 0. By F4, ∫_{M∩V} θ dH = 0, and θ > 0 on M, so H(M ∩ V) = 0. Removing an H-null set from M changes neither the integrals defining τ nor the blow-up integrals in HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt (blowUpMap x r maps H-null sets to H-null sets), and it preserves the other triple conditions.
(G3) Extension (P3). Fix once and for all χ ∈ C^∞(ℝ^P) with 0 ≤ χ ≤ 1, χ = 1 on an open neighbourhood N of K, and tsupport χ compact ⊆ U (smooth Urysohn, exists_contMDiffMap_one_nhds_of_subset_interior, applied to K and a compact neighbourhood of K inside U). For X ∈ D_k(U) with spt X ⊆ K define X̃(ω) := X(χω) for ω ∈ D^k(ℝ^P); note χω ∈ D^k(U). Then:
   (i) X̃ ∈ D_k(ℝ^P): it is linear, and if ω_q → 0 in D^k(ℝ^P) then χω_q → 0 in D^k(U) (supports in tsupport χ; Leibniz rule for iterated derivatives).
   (ii) X̃(ω) = X(ω) for ω ∈ D^k(U): tsupport((1 − χ)ω) ∩ K = ∅, so X((1 − χ)ω) = 0 by G1.
   (iii) If k ≥ 1 then ∂X̃ = (∂X)~, the extension of ∂X with the same χ (spt ∂X ⊆ K by G1). Indeed ∂X̃(ω) = X(χ dω) = X(d(χω)) − X(η) with η := d(χω) − χ dω ∈ D^k(U). By the Leibniz rule for fderiv, η(x) depends linearly on Dχ(x), so η = 0 on the open set N where χ ≡ 1. Hence tsupport η ⊆ ℝ^P ∖ N is disjoint from K, X(η) = 0 by G1, and ∂X̃(ω) = X(d(χω)) = ∂X(χω).
   (iv) M(X̃) ≤ M(X) and M(∂X̃) ≤ M(∂X): if ω is admissible on ℝ^P then χω is admissible on U (|χω| ≤ |ω| ≤ 1).
   (v) spt X̃ ⊆ K: if tsupport ω ∩ K = ∅ then X̃(ω) = X(χω) = 0 by G1.
   (vi) If X = τ(M, θ, ξ) is integer multiplicity in U, then by G2 and χ = 1 on K ⊇ spt X, X̃(ω) = ∫_{M∩spt X} θ ξ(χω) dH = ∫_{M∩spt X} θ ξ(ω) dH. The triple (M ∩ spt X, θ, ξ) is an integer multiplicity rectifiable triple in ℝ^P: integrability on compact subsets of ℝ^P follows from integrability on M ∩ K (K compact ⊆ U), and the tangent data are as in G2. So X̃ is integer multiplicity in ℝ^P.
(G4) Restriction to U (P3). For Y ∈ D_k(ℝ^P) let Y|_U := Y.restrictDomain (subset_univ U) ∈ D_k(U), so Y|_U(ω) = Y(ω). Then ∂(Y|_U) = (∂Y)|_U, and M(Y|_U) ≤ M(Y) since forms admissible on U are admissible on ℝ^P. If Y = τ(M, θ, ξ) is integer multiplicity in ℝ^P, then Y|_U = τ(M ∩ U, θ, ξ) is integer multiplicity in U. Indeed, for x ∈ M ∩ U, f ∈ C_c with spt f ⊆ B_R(0) and r < dist(x, ℝ^P ∖ U)/R, the blow-up integrals of (M ∩ U, θ) and (M, θ) at x coincide, because blowUpMap x r '' (M ∖ U) misses B_R(0). The other conditions are inherited.
(G5) Lattice chains (P4). Let ρ > 0, β : LatticeFaceIndex n P → ℝ and Pc ∈ D_n(ℝ^P) with IsLatticeChain ρ β Pc. For a face index F₀ = (z₀, α₀) let F̊₀ := {x : ρ z₀_i < x_i < ρ(z₀_i + 1) for i ∈ range α₀, x_i = ρ z₀_i otherwise}, the relative interior of latticeFace ρ F₀.
   - For p ∈ F̊₀ and 0 < σ < min(ρ, dist(p, latticeFace ρ F₀ ∖ F̊₀)), the ball B_σ(p) meets no face of direction α₀ other than latticeFace ρ F₀: faces of direction α₀ in the same affine n-plane meet latticeFace ρ F₀ only in its relative boundary, and faces of direction α₀ in other parallel planes are at distance ≥ ρ.
   - Let dx^{α₀} ∈ Λ^n be the covector with dx^{α₀}(e_α) = δ_{αα₀} for increasing α, so |ψ(x) dx^{α₀}| = |ψ(x)|. For ψ ∈ C_c^∞(B_σ(p)) and ω := ψ dx^{α₀}: latticeFaceAction ρ F ω = 0 for every F = (z, α) with α ≠ α₀ (since ω(x)(e_α) = 0), and for every F ≠ F₀ of direction α₀ (since ω vanishes on that face). So the tsum defining Pc(ω) has the single term Pc(ω) = β(F₀) ∫_{latticeFace ρ F₀} ψ dH.

H is preserved by isometries (Isometry.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image) and equals Lebesgue measure on ℝ^n, so H(latticeFace ρ F₀) = ρ^n, and H⌞F̊₀ charges every nonempty relatively open subset of F̊₀.
   Consequently, if β(F₀) ≠ 0:
   (a) Taking ψ ≥ 0 with ψ(p) > 0 gives Pc(ω) ≠ 0 for forms supported in arbitrarily small balls around p, so p ∈ spt Pc. Hence F̊₀ ⊆ spt Pc and latticeFace ρ F₀ = closure F̊₀ ⊆ closure(spt Pc).
   (b) Take compact sets C_q ↑ F̊₀ and ψ_q ∈ C_c^∞ with 0 ≤ ψ_q ≤ 1, ψ_q = 1 on C_q, and support in a neighbourhood of C_q meeting no other α₀-face. The forms ω_q := sign(β(F₀)) ψ_q dx^{α₀} are admissible, and Pc(ω_q) = |β(F₀)| ∫_{latticeFace ρ F₀} ψ_q dH, where H(C_q) ≤ ∫_{latticeFace ρ F₀} ψ_q dH ≤ H(latticeFace ρ F₀) = ρ^n and H(C_q) ↑ H(F̊₀) = ρ^n. Hence Pc(ω_q) → |β(F₀)| ρ^n, and |β(F₀)| ρ^n ≤ M(Pc).

1. (Approximation at scale ρ, case P ≥ n + 1: parent (P5) via DeformationTheorem.) Write P = n + ℓ = m + 1 + ℓ with ℓ ≥ 1 (transport all data along this equality of dimensions), and let C = C(m, ℓ) be given by DeformationTheorem. Fix ρ > 0. For each j let X_j := T̃_j (G3 with k = n). Then:
   - X_j ∈ D_n(ℝ^P) is integer multiplicity (G3(vi));
   - ∂X_j = (∂T_j)~ is integer multiplicity, by G3(iii) and G3(vi) applied to the integer multiplicity current ∂T_j, whose support lies in K by G1;
   - spt X_j ⊆ K, and M(X_j) + M(∂X_j) ≤ M(T_j) + M(∂T_j) ≤ B < ∞.
   DeformationTheorem gives Pc_j, β_j, R̃_j ∈ D_{n+1}(ℝ^P) and S̃_j ∈ D_n(ℝ^P) with:
   - IsLatticeChain ρ β_j Pc_j and X_j − Pc_j = ∂R̃_j + S̃_j;
   - M(Pc_j) ≤ C M(X_j) ≤ CB, M(R̃_j) ≤ Cρ M(X_j) ≤ CρB, M(S̃_j) ≤ Cρ M(∂X_j) ≤ CρB;
   - spt Pc_j ⊆ thickening(2√P ρ, spt X_j) ⊆ thickening(2√P ρ, K);
   - all β_j(F) ∈ ℤ, and R̃_j, S̃_j integer multiplicity (since X_j and ∂X_j are).
   Let Y_ρ := cthickening(2√P ρ, K), a bounded set, and 𝓕_ρ := {F : latticeFace ρ F ⊆ Y_ρ}, a finite set by G5(c). By G5(a), β_j(F) ≠ 0 implies latticeFace ρ F ⊆ closure(spt Pc_j) ⊆ Y_ρ, i.e. F ∈ 𝓕_ρ. By G5(b), |β_j(F)| ≤ M(Pc_j)/ρ^n ≤ CB/ρ^n. Hence β_j lies in 𝓑_ρ := {β : β(F) ∈ ℤ ∩ [−CB/ρ^n, CB/ρ^n] for F ∈ 𝓕_ρ, β(F) = 0 for F ∉ 𝓕_ρ}, a finite set independent of j. Put R_j := R̃_j|_U, S_j := S̃_j|_U and Q_j := Pc_j|_U (G4). Then R_j and S_j are integer multiplicity, T_j − Q_j = ∂R_j + S_j on D^n(U) (G3(ii), G4), and M(R_j) + M(S_j) ≤ 2CρB.

2. (Approximation at scale ρ, case P = n: printed (27)–(37) of 5.1 with Q := X, R := 0.) Fix ρ > 0 and let X_j := T̃_j ∈ D_n(ℝ^n) as in step 1: integer multiplicity, spt X_j ⊆ K, M(X_j) + M(∂X_j) ≤ B, and ∂X_j ∈ D_m(ℝ^n).
   (a) (Density; (27)–(28).) Write X_j = τ(M_j, θ_j, ξ_j) with H(M_j ∖ K) = 0 (G2, G3). For H-a.e. x ∈ M_j, ξ_j(x) = ±simpleNVector τ(x) for an orthonormal basis τ(x) of ℝ^n. Moreover simpleNVector τ = det[τ] · e with e := simpleNVector(e_1, …, e_n) and det[τ] = ±1 (multilinearity and alternation). So ξ_j = ε_j e with ε_j(x) ∈ {±1} a.e. on M_j. Put u_j := ε_j θ_j 1_{M_j}. Then u_j is integer-valued and integrable, u_j = 0 a.e. outside K, X_j(ω) = ∫ u_j(x) ω(x)(e_1, …, e_n) dx (H = μHE[n] is Lebesgue measure on ℝ^n), and M(X_j) = ∫ |u_j| dx (F4).
   (b) (Translation estimate.) For h ∈ ℝ^n, ∫ |u_j(x + h) − u_j(x)| dx ≤ |h| M(∂X_j).
   Proof: let g ∈ C_c^∞(ℝ^n) with |g| ≤ 1. By the fundamental theorem of calculus for t ↦ g(y − th) and Fubini (the integrand is bounded by sup|Dg| |h| |u_j|),
   ∫ (u_j(x + h) − u_j(x)) g(x) dx = ∫ u_j(y)(g(y − h) − g(y)) dy = −∫_0^1 ∫ u_j(y) ⟨Dg(y − th), h⟩ dy dt.
   For fixed t, ⟨Dg(y − th), h⟩ = div G_t(y) with G_t(y) := g(y − th) h ∈ C_c^∞(ℝ^n; ℝ^n). Let ω_t ∈ D^{n−1}(ℝ^n) be the (n−1)-form whose coefficient on the increasing (n−1)-tuple omitting e_i is ±G_t^i, with signs chosen so that dω_t(e_1, …, e_n) = div G_t for the convention exteriorDerivative = alternatizeUncurryFin ∘ fderiv. Then |ω_t(y)| = |G_t(y)| ≤ |h|, and ∫ u_j div G_t dy = X_j(dω_t) = ∂X_j(ω_t), so |∫ u_j div G_t dy| ≤ |h| M(∂X_j) (F3). Hence |∫ (u_j(· + h) − u_j) g| ≤ |h| M(∂X_j) for every such g. Approximate sign(u_j(· + h) − u_j) a.e. by such g (Lusin's theorem and mollification, truncated to |g| ≤ 1); dominated convergence gives the claim.
   (c) (Medians and the chain; (31), (35)–(36).) In ℝ^n the faces of 𝓛_n(ρ) are the cubes F_z := latticeFace ρ (z, id) = ρ(z + [0, 1]^n), z ∈ ℤ^n, since SimonMultiIndex n n consists of id only. For each z let β_z be an integer median of u_j on F_z, i.e. |F_z ∩ {u_j ≥ β_z}| ≥ ρ^n/2 and |F_z ∩ {u_j ≤ β_z}| ≥ ρ^n/2. Take β_z := the least integer k with |F_z ∩ {u_j ≤ k}| ≥ ρ^n/2, which exists because u_j is integer-valued and finite a.e. Then:
   - |β_z| ρ^n ≤ 2 ∫_{F_z} |u_j|: if β_z ≥ 1 then |u_j| ≥ β_z on a set of measure ≥ ρ^n/2, and symmetrically if β_z ≤ −1;
   - β_z ≠ 0 forces |F_z ∩ {u_j ≠ 0}| > 0, hence F_z ∩ K ≠ ∅ and F_z ⊆ cthickening(√n ρ, K);
   - since a median minimizes c ↦ ∫_{F_z} |u_j − c|, we have ∫_{F_z} |u_j − β_z| ≤ ∫_{F_z} |u_j − ū_z| ≤ ρ^{−n} ∫_{F_z} ∫_{F_z} |u_j(x) − u_j(y)| dy dx, where ū_z := ρ^{−n} ∫_{F_z} u_j.
   Let β_j(z, id) := β_z (finitely many nonzero), v_j := Σ_z β_z 1_{F̊_z}, and Pc_j(ω) := Σ_z β_z latticeFaceAction ρ (z, id) ω = ∫ v_j(x) ω(x)(e_1, …, e_n) dx (cube boundaries are null). Then:
   - Pc_j ∈ D_n(ℝ^n), IsLatticeChain ρ β_j Pc_j, and M(Pc_j) ≤ Σ_z |β_z| ρ^n ≤ 2 ∫ |u_j| = 2M(X_j) ≤ 2B;
   - Pc_j is integer multiplicity: Pc_j = τ(M_P, |v_j|, sign(v_j) e), where M_P := ⋃_{β_z ≠ 0} F̊_z is open and contained in ℝ^n = range(id) (countably n-rectifiable). At each x ∈ M_P, |v_j| is constant near x, so the blow-ups of (M_P, |v_j|) at x converge to |v_j(x)| H⌞ℝ^n; thus ℝ^n = span(e_1, …, e_n) is the weighted approximate tangent space, and sign(v_j(x)) e = ±simpleNVector(e_1, …, e_n).
   (d) (The Poincaré inequality (32), summed over the cubes.) The cubes overlap only in null sets and diam F_z = √n ρ, so by (c) and (b):
   Σ_z ∫_{F_z} |u_j − β_z| ≤ ρ^{−n} ∫∫_{|x − y| ≤ √n ρ} |u_j(x) − u_j(y)| dy dx = ρ^{−n} ∫_{|h| ≤ √n ρ} ∫ |u_j(x + h) − u_j(x)| dx dh ≤ ρ^{−n} · |B_{√n ρ}| · √n ρ · M(∂X_j) ≤ c_n ρ B,
   with c_n := ω_n n^{(n+1)/2}. (Simon obtains (32) cube by cube from the BV Poincaré inequality of Ch. 2, 2.7; only the summed form is used here, and the translation estimate (b) gives it directly.)
   (e) Put R̃_j := 0 ∈ D_{n+1}(ℝ^n) and S̃_j := X_j − Pc_j, integer multiplicity by the sibling im_lincomb. Then X_j − Pc_j = ∂R̃_j + S̃_j, and M(S̃_j) ≤ ∫ |u_j − v_j| = Σ_z ∫_{F_z} |u_j − β_z| ≤ c_n ρ B, since S̃_j(ω) = ∫ (u_j − v_j) ω(x)(e_1, …, e_n) dx and |ω(x)(e_1, …, e_n)| ≤ |ω(x)|.
   (f) If β_j(z, id) ≠ 0 then F_z ⊆ cthickening(√n ρ, K) (finitely many z) and |β_j(z, id)| ≤ 2B/ρ^n. So β_j lies in a finite set 𝓑_ρ independent of j. Put R_j := 0 ∈ D_{n+1}(U), S_j := S̃_j|_U and Q_j := Pc_j|_U (G4). Then R_j and S_j are integer multiplicity, T_j − Q_j = ∂R_j + S_j on D^n(U), and M(R_j) + M(S_j) ≤ c_n ρ B.

3. (Pigeonhole; parent Step 5.) Let C' := max(2C, c_n), or C' := c_n if P = n. In both cases, for every ρ > 0 and every j:
   - β_j ∈ 𝓑_ρ (a finite set);
   - Q_j(ω) = Σ'_F β_j(F) latticeFaceAction ρ F ω for ω ∈ D^n(U);
   - R_j, S_j are integer multiplicity with T_j − Q_j = ∂R_j + S_j and M(R_j) + M(S_j) ≤ C' ρ B.
   Given ε > 0 and an infinite J ⊆ ℕ, choose ρ > 0 with 2C'ρB < ε (possible since B < ∞). The map j ↦ β_j sends the infinite set J into the finite set 𝓑_ρ, so by the pigeonhole principle some fiber J' := {j ∈ J : β_j = β*} is infinite. For i, j ∈ J', Q_i = Q_j (same coefficients), hence T_i − T_j = ∂(R_i − R_j) + (S_i − S_j) on D^n(U). R := R_i − R_j and S := S_i − S_j are integer multiplicity (sibling im_lincomb with a = 1, b = −1), and M(R) + M(S) ≤ M(R_i) + M(R_j) + M(S_i) + M(S_j) ≤ 2C'ρB < ε (F2). ∎
proof_key_steps: P < m + 1: all currents of degree m + 1 and m + 2 vanish; take R = S = 0.
Support, extension and restriction calculus: extend T_j to ℝ^P with a cutoff χ (integer multiplicity, same mass and boundary mass, support in K) and restrict outputs back to U.
P ≥ m + 2: DeformationTheorem at scale ρ; lattice-chain facts (β_F ≠ 0 ⇒ face ⊆ closure spt Pc, and |β_F|ρ^n ≤ M(Pc)) put the coefficient vectors in a finite set.
P = m + 1: printed (27)–(37) of 5.1 — integer medians on lattice cubes, Pc := Σβ_F[[F]], R := 0, S := X − Pc, M(Pc) ≤ 2M(X), and M(S) ≤ c_nρM(∂X) via the translation estimate.
Pigeonhole on the coefficient vectors: T_i − T_j = ∂(R_i − R_j) + (S_i − S_j), integer multiplicity by im_lincomb, with mass ≤ 2C'ρB < ε.

audit.reason: The contract includes compact support, finite uniform mass, and integrality of currents and boundaries. Extension and domain restriction preserve the needed properties. Deformation gives finitely many coefficient vectors in positive codimension; the supplied translation estimate and integer medians cover P = m + 1. Pigeonhole and integer differences then give the stated global mass bound, including the trivial-dimensional cases.
